task: When a declared LiteLLM auto-router has no max_output_tokens, set it at catalog load to the smallest positive max_output_tokens among its tier models, so codemie forwards max_tokens for router requests (EPMCDME-16835).

key_reasoning.reason: The change copies the LLMService._router_max_input_tokens pattern: resolve tiers by base_name and take the minimum. The forwarding in llm_factory (_resolve_max_output_tokens / _build_chat_model_base_args) already handles a positive max_output_tokens and stays unchanged. LLM_PROXY_FORWARD_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS can turn it off. The one real correctness risk is sending a value above some tier's limit, and taking the minimum across all tiers prevents that. Other residual risks: the Claude-name gate on the router alias, and the lazy-import rule against circular imports.

Scope, out-of-scope items and acceptance criteria are explicit: forward max_tokens = min tier max_output_tokens, an explicit router value still wins, and regression tests cover derivation and forwarding. Two small policy choices are left: for unknown or disabled tiers, use the minimum over the known tiers or return None conservatively (the max_input_tokens precedent), and whether to log the derivation.
